topic.title: The Toy That Sold 100 Million Copies by Dying

title: Why Did Kids Love Tamagotchi, a Toy That Could Die?
description:
Why would a keyring pet that dies if you forget it become one of the best-selling toys ever?
Tamagotchi, 1996 to 2025, told from Bandai Namco's own figures.
Sources: Bandai Namco Holdings (Jul 2025).
Based on public records and reporting. Not financial or legal advice.

cta: Fed it on time or let it die: which kid were you? Comment

lines.text: Tamagotchi could die in your pocket, and kids still lined up to own one.
Bandai put it on sale in Japan in November 1996. In eight months, Japan bought about 10M of them.
The trick was the pet inside. It got hungry, it got sick, and if you forgot it, it died.
Crazes like that fade fast. So why didn't this one?
Bandai kept bringing it back in new shapes, with colour screens and new pets to raise.
And it left Japan. By Bandai's count, 51% of all of them went to buyers outside the country.
By July last year, Bandai had shipped 100M Tamagotchis. A pet that dies, and still sells.
Fed it on time, or let it die: which kid were you? Either way, it was a Tamagotchi.

Re-review of changed lines. Hook 'kids still lined up to own one': queues at Japanese stores in the 1996-97 boom are reported by the South China Morning Post (early-morning queues at stores rumoured to have stock) and Smithsonian Magazine (shoppers waiting outside stores for shipments); those reports name parents as well as kids. The question label sub 'and then they are gone' is general framing and claims no fact. The swapped pictures are Commons photos of Tamagotchi models and Tamagotchi shops, with no captions that claim facts. The earlier pass on all 4 Bandai Namco facts and the disclaimer still stands.

'By July last year' is right as of Nov 2026. Colour screen (Plus Color 2008) and new versions are on the same page. No advice, the tone is fine, and the description ends with the disclaimer. Notes: the world beat's document lines paraphrase the newsletter rather than quote it; the hook's 'exactly why kids wanted one' and the label 'most within a year or two' are framing, not sourced.
